scope: Unreleased delta since 2026.10.15.2 (PR #12): the new read-only `prime` method, its `primeContext` resource and schema, PrimeArgsSchema flag mapping, README/manifest updates, and tests. Post-merge hardening from this review: maxMemoryChars is documented as bd's byte cap, the agent.profile parse now searches only the policy text before the appended memories, two tests cover explicit and implicit profiles, and the deno-command quality acceptance is recorded on runBd. Existing methods, resources, global args, and the bd-usable check are unchanged.

dimensions.note: No credential handling added. prime shells out to the local bd CLI only. The captured text may contain project memories, which bd already persists; the resource stores no environment, tokens, or config beyond that text.

Single structured log line: 'Captured bd prime context ({chars} chars, profile {profile})' with placeholder props. It logs length and profile only, not the captured content, so memories are not duplicated into logs. Failures go through runBdStrict, which logs exit code and truncated stderr/stdout.

prime uses runBdStrict, so a nonzero bd exit throws 'bd prime failed (exit N)' with stderr/stdout, matching every other method. Number flags are z.number().int().min(0) and stringified from validated values, so malformed input is rejected before spawn. Empty stdout after a successful exit writes an empty content string rather than throwing; acceptable for a context capture.

Suite: 21 passed against the real bd CLI in throwaway projects. New: a create dedup test asserts the second create returns the same issue id and that labels round-trip through list. Existing prime tests (5) and the create/show/update/close, list/ready, query, dep, reopen, reclaim, graph, and failure-path tests still pass. Not separately asserted: multi-label dedup beyond one label (the helper checks every label in the set) and the 500-issue list cap.

create is now idempotent on the caller-controlled (labels, title, status=open) tuple: normalizeIssue preserves labels, and create searches bd list --label before creating, returning the existing issue and its resource instead of a duplicate. Callers that want per-fire uniqueness vary the title. Other methods remain read-only or single-resource upserts. A failed bd call still throws before writeResource, so no half-written resource is left behind.

Flag mapping verified against `bd prime --help`: memories include/only/exclude maps to no flag/--memories-only/--no-memories; maxMemories and maxMemoryChars map to --max-memories/--max-memory-chars, with explicit 0 forcing unlimited. maxMemoryChars is now described as bd's byte cap rather than characters. The profile parse searches only the text before the appended memories heading, so a memory quoting agent.profile= cannot be mistaken for the active policy; default bd output prints no explicit profile, which correctly yields null.

runBd still uses Deno.Command().output(), which drains and closes stdout/stderr on every call; prime adds no handles, temp files, or watchers. The quality acceptance comment documents why the bd subprocess is the contract rather than a bypass.
README additions use the existing my-tracker/placeholder style and show only literal JSON inputs. No tokens, hostnames, local paths, or account identifiers are added to README, manifest, or tests.

PrimeArgsSchema and PrimeContextSchema are plain z.object schemas with no passthrough. Objects are validated with .parse at the method boundary, so unknown keys are stripped before reaching bd or the resource store, consistent with the other argument schemas.

primeContext uses the same lifetime 30d / garbageCollection 10 as issue and dependencyGraph. Because there is one fixed instance, retention stays at one live resource; 30d is generous but harmless for a text snapshot of a few KB.

prime is an intentional read-only capture, like ready/query/graph; it adds no update or delete surface for a value derived from the CLI. Existing CRUD for issues is unchanged, so no new gap is introduced.

The unchanged bd-usable dependency check still fronts every method, so prime fails cleanly with bd's exit code/stderr when the CLI or database is missing. prime adds no new prerequisite beyond bd and a .beads database, which the README states.

primeContext writes a single `prime-current` instance by design (same pattern as dependencyGraph's fixed instance). It cannot collide with issue instance names because resources are namespaced by spec. Repeated runs overwrite in place.

No direct dataRepository access and no cached reads; prime always re-runs bd so the captured context reflects the current PRIME.md, config, and memories. That matches the extension's projection-of-bd model.

Upgrades entries exist through 2026.10.21.1 (a no-op passthrough for the create-idempotency change). The model source version, manifest version, and upgrade entry now agree at 2026.10.21.1; the previous release left model.version at 2026.10.16.1 while the manifest had moved.
